from.place: the final base-change and quotient-completeness argument

title: Complete local base change and closed-fibre identification
statement: Let R,A,T be commutative local rings, with T Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and complete for its maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Let q:R\twoheadrightarrow A and f:R\to T be local ring maps. Let E be a commutative A-algebra and e:T/m_R T\cong E a ring isomorphism such that e(f(r)\bmod m_R T)=q(r) in E for every r. Then C=T\otimes_R A with the canonical right A-algebra structure is Noetherian complete local, A\to C is local, the image of m_T generates m_C, and C/m_A C\cong E as A-algebras.

source.place: More on Algebra, Tag 07NR (lemma-lift-fs), the final base-change and quotient-completeness argument

proof.text: Set I=ker q. Surjectivity gives A ≅ R/I, and the tensor-quotient isomorphism identifies C with T/IT. Locality implies I lies in m_R and IT lies in m_T. Quotient completeness yields the Noetherian complete local structure and maximal ideal formula.

source.place: More on Algebra, Tag 07NR (lemma-lift-fs), the final base-change and quotient-completeness argument

proof.text: A surjective local map carries m_R onto m_A. Therefore A → C is local, m_A C is the image of m_R T, and quotienting C by m_A C gives T/m_R T. Compose with e. Lift each a in A to r in R and use compatibility of e to check A-linearity of the ring isomorphism.
